implementation_notes: Implemented DispatchSemaphore as a pure-counter wrapper guarded by threading.Lock rather than holding an inner asyncio.Semaphore. Rationale (carried forward from the prior turn's player_summary in the task front-matter): the brief mentions 'thin wrapper around asyncio.Semaphore' in prose, but the embedded Implementation Notes explicitly recommend maintaining an explicit counter rather than touching _value, because asyncio.Semaphore exposes no public non-blocking acquire path (only async acquire and the binary locked()), and its internal _value is private and varies across Python versions. A threading.Lock keeps the wrapper safe for the routing-history writer's worker thread without inheriting asyncio loop affinity. Public surface matches API-internal.md §5 exactly: __init__(*, cap=8) with ValueError on cap<1, try_acquire() -> bool (synchronous, increments in_flight on True, returns False without mutation on overflow), release() (idempotent — early-return when in_flight<=0, never raises, never underflows), in_flight property, plus a cap property for diagnostics. Module docstring records the deviation from the literal asyncio.Semaphore wrapper sketch and cross-references DDR-020. No changes to src/jarvis/infrastructure/__init__.py — the class is imported directly by future call sites (TASK-J004-010 dispatch.py snapshots and TASK-J004-013 lifecycle wiring) per the API-internal.md §6 'Snapshots dispatch_semaphore into dispatch.py module attributes' direction; broadening the package __all__ now would couple this task to those downstream changes.
